description: Editable rules for tagging catalog result columns. Exact overrides win; patterns are evaluated in order. Label columns (geography, theme, focus area, scheme, status) land on 'dimension', money on 'additive_value', counts on 'additive_count', and anything averaged/per-unit/percentage on 'ratio' so the operations layer refuses to sum it over the displayed rows. The 'ratio' classification is the load-bearing one: summing a column of percentages down a displayed table produces a confident number that means nothing.
_comment_prdw: The exact entries and the first three pattern rules below were added for the Odisha PR&DW catalogue. The rest are the generic rules inherited from the AP build; they are kept because they are generic (name/status/date/code/money wording is not domain-specific) and because pruning working rules to tidy up is how a classifier quietly starts returning 'unclassified'.

exact._comment_prdw_aggregated_labels: STRING_AGG'd lists, not counts. Each needs an exact entry because the count patterns would otherwise claim it on a plural stem — 'activity_codes' on the code rule, 'schemes' and 'years' on the countable-things rule. Summing a comma-joined list is not an error anyone would catch by reading the answer.
exact._comment_entity_grain: Columns introduced when the entity-listing templates were collapsed to one row per farmer (fidelity item 2). The STRING_AGG'd label lists are dimensions; the per-entity counters are counts. Several need an exact entry because a pattern would otherwise claim them for the wrong family — 'registrations' contains the substring 'ratio', 'unpaid_deliveries' contains 'paid', and the '*_transactions' pair contains 'subsidy'.
exact._comment_new_templates: Columns introduced by the templates added in the same pass (Q147-Q153, F13, G46). 'declared_over_recorded' is the P11 over-declaration ratio; 'state_schemes' is a scheme count that the dimension pattern would otherwise claim on the word 'state'.
exact._comment_money_vs_status: Money columns the status-prefix rule claims first. '(^|_)(started|ongoing|completed|approved|abandoned|awaiting)_' sits above the money rule on purpose -- 'gps_approved' is a count of gram panchayats, not an amount -- so these are pinned here rather than by reordering the patterns, which would break that. The '_year1'/'_year2' pair is claimed by a different clause in the same rule; 'expenditure_year1' is SUM(v.total_expenditure) FILTER (...), so it is an amount too.
exact._comment_per_unit_means: Per-unit MEANS, not totals: SUM(cost)/COUNT(*), expenditure/gps, and AVG(...) OVER (). They were classified additive_count, which offers them for summation -- and summing a per-activity average down a displayed table is exactly the confident, meaningless number this file exists to prevent. They are ratios, like avg_planned_cost.

patterns._comment: Derived measures announce themselves in their prefix — catch them before anything else can claim the stem ('pct_mobile' is a rate, not an identifier).
PR&DW: percentage-point deviations. Anchored and placed above the count rules, which would otherwise never see it — but it must also stay below the pct_ prefix rule.

PR&DW: the counted nouns of this domain. GRAM PANCHAYATS in every shape the catalogue counts them ('gps_uploaded', 'late_gps', 'gps_with_plan'), ACTIVITIES ditto ('planned_activities', 'matching_activities', 'activities_year1', 'change_in_activities'), and the year/status counters. Above the money and label rules because several of these contain a money or label word — 'sc_targeted_activities' holds no rupees, and 'gps_approved' is a count and not a status.
PR&DW: expenditure written short. The generic money rule catches 'expenditure' and 'cost'; the catalogue also abbreviates ('maintenance_exp', 'fresh_exp') and uses bare 'spent'.
Cardinality prefixes are counts whatever they count ('distinct_aadhaar', 'values_found', 'missing_khata').
Dates — anchored so 'PAYMENT_DATE', 'SurveyDate', 'survey_month' and 'latest_installment' are temporal but 'STATUS_UPDATE' is not.
Identifiers: codes, account/reference numbers, Aadhaar, mobile, khata, survey number, IFSC.
Rates, averages and per-unit measures. 'tat'/'lag'/'days'/'share' are anchored — unanchored they matched 'status', 'village' and 'shared_farmers'.
Label columns: personal and place names, and the closed-vocabulary attributes the catalog groups by.
Countable things and physical quantities — safe to sum across the rows of the displayed table.
Anything left that reads like a label.
